First verify the target position's school level, curriculum, teacher qualification, school hiring, and program authorization, as well as class hours, class size, tools, and site conditions. In China, qualification application follows the rule that a qualification covers the same level and below, with separate mutual recognition between senior secondary and secondary vocational qualifications, and practicum supervision has its own limits; check against the specific provisions and the recruitment notice. Pause large investments until this is clear — paper exercises do not equal authorization to teach.

Low-cost trial: using the fictional paper-bridge curriculum standard, class profile, materials, and three performance records from the T1 pathway, design two lessons, compute rubric scores, log the missing evidence, and handle the injected hazard. Pen and paper are enough — no real students, no operating tools. Keep the lesson plans, assessments, and revision records, and observe whether you want to keep exploring.

Signals to keep exploring: willingness to explain repeatedly for different ability levels, to accept scrutiny of task design and scoring, and to record the process honestly; being able to stop and re-verify without glossing over it when materials are hazardous or evidence is missing. First look at the lesson plans, scoring rationale, and exception states in the T1 work; these are task-exploration clues, not proof of competence in a real classroom.

Verify education, professional certification, teacher qualification, and school authorization separately. In the O*NET education survey, 86% say new hires need a bachelor's, 6% a high school diploma, and 3% a post-baccalaureate certificate — this is not the actual educational composition of the workforce or a China threshold. National Board certification is professional recognition, and the conditions for starting versus earning it differ; in China, qualifications follow the same-level-and-below, senior-secondary/secondary-vocational mutual recognition, and practicum supervision exceptions — check the current provisions and the recruitment notice.

This is a role that turns middle school students' understanding of occupational or technical fields and their safe task process into reviewable evidence: curriculum objectives, material checks, process assessment, scoring rationale, performance and attendance, and exception records. Teachers handle these per their duties and carry the student-protection reporting obligation; in China the statutory immediate external report cannot be replaced by internal school processes alone. Chinese enterprise teaching staff wages are a broad proxy, not this occupation's wages.

The work of this occupation falls into three categories: first, career and technical course teaching (breaking occupational exploration and technical introduction into age-appropriate tasks, preparing materials and task contexts, lecturing, demonstrating, and guiding students' hands-on work, and assessing by process and product); second, materials, equipment, and classroom safety (preparing and maintaining tools and materials, spelling out prohibited actions and safety checks, circulating and correcting while students work, and establishing and enforcing classroom order rules); third, assessment, records, and communication (observing and evaluating student performance and behavior, maintaining student records and attendance, communicating with parents or guardians, colleagues, and administrators, and participating in individualized support, tutoring, and referrals). All three share the same chain centered on age-appropriate tasks, safety conditions, and student evidence.
Career and technical course teaching

Break occupational processes into age-appropriate tasks and learning objectives → prepare materials, task contexts, and demonstration steps → explain and demonstrate and organize students' hands-on practice → assess by process and product and give feedback → adjust difficulty and provide differentiated support based on assessment results → document teaching and student progress
Materials, equipment, and classroom safety

Suggestions for organizing practical training: verify tools, materials, and site conditions, and demonstrate and supervise safe use; Article 18 of China's school safety measures requires that facilities with hidden hazards be taken out of use and repaired, replaced, guarded, or marked with warnings; specific equipment repair and restoration are determined by the school's division-of-labor system and cannot be granted by this page. Provide timely aid after an injury — recording and reporting must not be delayed.

Collect evidence of student process and products → score against the published scoring dimensions and state the rationale → maintain student records and attendance → communicate progress and improvement points with parents or guardians → collaborate with colleagues and counselors and administrators on individual needs → report exceptions per procedure and keep records

Middle school career and technical education teachers center on occupational exploration and technical learning outcomes in the intermediate grades; general middle school teachers focus on subject courses, education administrators handle school-level curriculum and personnel decisions, educational guidance and career counselors address students' further-education and career counseling, and computer science teachers and education teachers and family and consumer sciences teachers at the higher education stage focus on subject teaching and research. Similar names or adjacency in the education chain do not mean that teacher qualification, teaching level and subject scope, assessment authority, and student-protection handling authority are interchangeable.
Core purpose

To give middle school students age-appropriate, safe, and assessable hands-on experience and occupational awareness in an occupational or technical field: age-appropriate tasks and learning objectives keep the content understandable, process assessment and records keep learning visible and reviewable, and safety checks and order management keep the process controllable.
Main subjects and basis

The subjects are middle school students and classes and small groups, as well as curriculum standards and textbooks and task designs, tools and materials and protective equipment and classrooms and laboratories and workshop sites, process and product assessment criteria and scoring rationale, enrollment and grade and attendance and communication records, and individualized support and tutoring and extracurricular activity arrangements; the basis is the local teacher qualification and teaching scope rules, school and district policies and administrative regulations, curriculum standards and teaching syllabi, tool and material and site safety requirements, student record and privacy and mandatory reporting requirements, and the school's approval system for courses and activities.
Core process

Design age-appropriate tasks and objectives, prepare materials and sites, explain and demonstrate, organize and circulate during student practice, assess by process and product and give feedback, document student progress, communicate with parents and colleagues, and report exceptions per procedure.
Main outputs

Curriculum objectives and task contexts and teaching materials, process assessment rubrics and scoring rationale, student performance and attendance and enrollment records, tool and material and site inspection and maintenance records, communication records with students and parents or guardians, individualized support and tutoring and extracurricular activity records, and exception and reporting records.
Accountable parties

In mainland China, when a minor's physical or mental health is harmed, suspected of being harmed, or at risk, a report must be made immediately to public security, civil affairs, education, and other relevant departments under Article 11 of the Law on the Protection of Minors; internal reporting cannot replace that statutory duty. Protect the student first, record faithfully, handle what falls within your duties, and do not conduct unauthorized investigations or disclose to unrelated persons. Reporting routes in the United States are verified separately under state law and school policy.
Authority and approval

Article 11 of China's Teachers Law requires a normal-school junior college diploma or other associate degree or above for culture and specialized course qualifications for junior secondary schools and junior vocational schools; Articles 4 and 5 of the qualification regulations distinguish teacher categories and in principle allow teaching at the same level and below, with mutual recognition between senior secondary and secondary vocational qualifications and separate limits for practicum supervisors; the actual subject, certification, and hiring are verified separately. Teaching, hiring, curriculum, and facility conditions are verified separately; Article 18 of China's school safety measures requires that facilities with hidden hazards be taken out of use and repaired, replaced, guarded, or marked with warnings; specific equipment repair and restoration are determined by the school's division-of-labor system and cannot be granted by this page. Provide timely aid after an injury — recording and reporting must not be delayed. Article 11 of China's Law on the Protection of Minors requires units in close contact with minors and their staff to report immediately to public security, civil affairs, education, and other relevant departments upon discovering harm, suspected harm, or other danger, and internal school reporting cannot replace or delay this; Articles 48 and 49 of the school protection regulations require timely handling within one's duties, external reporting when necessary, and timely aid, and must not wait for internal school approval first. U.S. obligations are verified separately under state law.
Conclusion boundaries

Curriculum records and assessment results describe how a student performed under the given curriculum standard, class profile, and teaching conditions; they are not a final characterization of the student's ability, nor do they replace the school's and competent authority's handling of student-protection matters, and they are updated as curriculum standards, class composition, and teaching arrangements change; when citing, state the curriculum standard version, the assessment method, and the record period at the same time.

Before starting, verify at least six items: job duties (leaning toward career and technical course teaching, materials and equipment and classroom safety, student guidance and individualized support, curriculum and program design, or teaching-research collaboration), the required teacher qualification and teaching level and subject scope, the available tools and sites and equipment conditions and the division of safety responsibility, class size and class hours and workload arrangements, student record and communication and mandatory reporting requirements, and whether the role includes homeroom or extracurricular activity or school-enterprise cooperation duties.
Occupational framing

This page's identity is U.S. O*NET-SOC25-2023.00, and the Chinese name does not prove a corresponding Chinese subcategory. The current round of occupational classification publication entries is not sufficient to establish a one-to-one mapping, and non-existence cannot be inferred from the absence of an established mapping. Article 4 of mainland China's Regulations on Teacher Qualifications includes culture and specialized course qualifications for junior secondary schools and junior vocational schools; Article 5 allows teaching at the same level and below, with mutual recognition between senior secondary and secondary vocational teacher qualifications, and separate limits for practicum supervisors. Qualification categories, teaching subjects, recruitment conditions, and school program authorization are verified separately, and this must not be written as requiring re-obtaining a qualification for every lower school level.
Education and training pathways

The O*NET Job Zone4 is a cross-occupational preparation zone; 86% bachelor's, 6% high school, and 3% post-baccalaureate certificate are answers about new-hire education requirements, not the incumbent educational composition or a legal condition. The summary is only an apprenticeship exploration entry and lists no specific program for this occupation; the training directory has 452 school programs, and the number of graduates does not equal the educational attainment of practitioners. The certification directory has 1 entry, the NBPTS CTE professional certification, which is not a uniform entry requirement. U.S. BLS summarizes the commonly required bachelor's degree and work experience in the field taught, and public school state licensure or certification is verified per state route; professional certification and licensure and school hiring are judged separately. Article 11 of China's Teachers Law requires a normal-school junior college diploma or other associate degree or above for culture and specialized course qualifications for junior secondary schools and junior vocational schools; Articles 4 and 5 of the qualification regulations distinguish teacher categories and in principle allow teaching at the same level and below, with mutual recognition between senior secondary and secondary vocational qualifications and separate limits for practicum supervisors; the actual subject, certification, and hiring are verified separately.
Methods and tools

The O*NET technology list names 33 categories of software skills, and the Hot Technologies page lists 69 items (including data analysis and visualization and SAS, cloud and containers and version control and programming languages); that page does not give each one's share (the data source is 2025 U.S. job postings from Lightcast); the list is very broad and mainly indicates that the occupation may require a variety of teaching and information technology tools in job postings — it does not mean every position needs all of them, nor does it represent an automation rate or job displacement. On-site methods and tools center on the tools and materials and protective equipment used in technical courses, classroom lecturing and demonstration equipment, learning management and grade and attendance record systems, process and product assessment tools, and curriculum standards and textbooks and task design materials.
Safety and work permits

Work is mainly fixed in-school schedules and being on site, while also carrying after-class workload such as lesson preparation and material preparation and grading and communication; the main load comes from standing and talking for long periods, continuous interpersonal interaction and emotional labor, and simultaneously watching several students' safety while using tools and materials. O*NET work context shows: 97% indoors in a controlled environment every day; 69% standing about half the time; 67% making a public speech every day; 67% facing time pressure at least once a week but not every day; 65% working more than 40 hours per week; 60% considering working with a team extremely important; 58% in continuous contact with others; 55% having face-to-face discussions every day; 51% having telephone conversations at least once a month but not every week; 50% keeping a moderate close distance (within arm's reach) with others; 47% dealing with unpleasant or angry or discourteous people every day; 47% reporting some freedom in making decisions; 46% considering coordinating or leading others extremely important; 46% exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise at least once a week but not every day; 45% making decisions every day that affect others or organizational resources or reputation; 33% having extremely high responsibility for the health and safety of other workers. Work requirements follow curriculum standards and school policy, and using tools and materials must follow safety procedures for protection and supervision; when a student safety anomaly is found, protect the student first and then report.
Training and regulatory requirements

U.S. public school licensure is verified per state, and private school requirements differ; in mainland China, teacher qualification is verified according to law. Article 4 of mainland China's Regulations on Teacher Qualifications includes culture and specialized course qualifications for junior secondary schools and junior vocational schools; Article 5 allows teaching at the same level and below, with mutual recognition between senior secondary and secondary vocational teacher qualifications, and separate limits for practicum supervisors. Qualification categories, teaching subjects, recruitment conditions, and school program authorization are verified separately, and this must not be written as requiring re-obtaining a qualification for every lower school level. Qualification does not equal school hiring, equipment conditions, or authorization for a specific program.
Pay and hours

U.S. 2025 median annual wage for this occupation is 65,030 USD, with P10—P90 at 49,200—101,890 USD, annual only. For U.S. 25-2023 middle school CTE teachers, BLS Table 1.2: employment is shown as 16,600 in both 2025 and 2035, a change rate of -0.5%, a net change of about -100, with about 1,000 annual openings (including replacement needs, not net new). Each figure is rounded independently, and the headcounts shown at the two ends cannot be subtracted to infer a net change. The current O*NET projection is also for 2025—2035, showing a change rate of -1%; this page keeps the precision of Table 1.2, and projections are not evidence of AI causation. China's 2025 enterprise teaching staff proxy median is 5.31 ten thousand yuan/year, with P10—P90 at 3—13.33 ten thousand yuan/year, not a public middle school or exact occupation wage. The NBS 2025 education sector urban non-private average pretax annual wage is 133,539 yuan and the private average is 63,908 yuan, both covering multiple occupations, not this occupation's average or median or starting or monthly wage; they are shown separately from the enterprise teaching staff wage percentile proxies. Class hours, workload, and holidays are verified separately.

This page's entry corresponds to career/technical education teachers, middle school (O*NET-SOC 25-2023.00): teaching occupational, vocational, career, or technical subjects to students at the middle school level (middle or intermediate grades or junior high school), with common fields including agricultural technology, business, computers, home economics, and industrial technology. Daily work includes: using multiple teaching methods such as lecture, discussion, and demonstration to provide individual and group instruction to students; preparing materials and the classroom for classroom activities; establishing and enforcing behavioral rules and procedures that maintain student order; adjusting teaching methods and instructional materials to meet students' varying needs and interests; using computers, audiovisual aids, and other equipment and materials to supplement presentations; instructing and monitoring students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injuries and damage; setting clear objectives for all lessons and units and projects and communicating those objectives to students; observing and evaluating students' performance and behavior and social development and physical health; assigning and grading class work and homework; maintaining accurate and complete student records as required by law and district policy and administrative regulations; instructing and counseling students with adjustment or academic problems or special academic interests; preparing students for later educational experiences by encouraging them to explore learning opportunities and to persevere with challenging tasks; planning and conducting a balanced program of instruction and demonstration and work time that provides students with opportunities to observe and question and investigate; meeting with parents or guardians to discuss their children's progress and to determine priorities and resource needs; enforcing all administrative policies and rules governing students; preparing and administering and grading tests and assignments to evaluate students' progress; conferring with parents or guardians and other teachers and counselors and administrators to resolve students' behavioral and academic problems; preparing and implementing remedial programs for students requiring extra help; meeting with other professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress; preparing assigned courses and providing written evidence of preparation as required by the direct supervisor; planning and supervising class projects and field trips and guest lectures and other experiential activities and guiding students in learning from them; preparing reports on students and activities as required by administration; providing assistive devices and supportive technology and assistance accessing facilities to students with disabilities; establishing course objectives and outlines following curriculum guidelines or requirements of the state and school; selecting and storing and ordering and issuing and inventorying and maintaining classroom equipment and materials and supplies; collaborating with other teachers and administrators in the development and evaluation and revision of middle school programs; meeting with other staff members to plan and schedule lessons following approved curricula; attending professional meetings and educational conferences and teacher training workshops to maintain and improve professional competence; attending staff meetings and serving on committees as required; sponsoring extracurricular activities such as student clubs and student organizations and academic competitions; and performing administrative duties such as library assistance and hallway and cafeteria monitoring and bus loading and unloading. It carries responsibility for student protection and teaching quality and teaching scope, but does not replace the school's and competent authority's responsibility for curriculum approval and the handling of student-protection matters and personnel management.

U.S. wages (the O*NET and BLS framing shown on this occupation's page): the BLS 2025 OEWS data displayed by O*NET give this occupation (25-2023.00) a national median annual wage of 65,030 USD; the 10th and 25th and 75th and 90th percentiles of annual wages are 49,200 and 58,690 and 79,990 and 101,890 USD. This round's national wage percentile page provides only the annual wage distribution and does not publish the hourly distribution, so this page does not derive hourly values from other framings and registers the hourly position as a visible gap in the fact register. The median means half of workers earn above and half below that value; it is not an entry-level wage or a starting-salary promise; the occupation typically requires obtaining the local teacher qualification limited by school level and subject, and wage percentiles do not represent an individual's job offer.

Mainland China side: this evidence route has not established a mainland China occupation-level wage distribution that precisely corresponds to O*NET-SOC 25-2023.00; the available official enterprise compensation survey only reaches the parent grouping 'enterprise teaching staff' (a broad proxy for enterprise teaching staff, 2025, median wage level 5.31 ten thousand yuan/year, 10th and 90th percentiles 3.00 ten thousand and 13.33 ten thousand yuan/year); this page publishes that figure as a parent-level proxy and marks at each place that it is a proxy framing rather than this occupation's exact framing, does not use industry averages to fill in, and does not convert U.S. figures into yuan; it also notes that the junior secondary school teacher qualification and the secondary vocational school specialized course and practicum supervision teacher qualifications are different categories and cannot be mapped directly from a U.S. occupation name. paragraphs: This page compares middle school career and technical education teachers with six adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference is a better fit for. Adjacent directions are described by their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean that job titles or teacher qualifications are interchangeable.

Evidence note: occupational direction and core outputs are based on O*NET-SOC 25-2023.00 and the official descriptions of adjacent entries (U.S. framing); the adjacent occupations listed by this evidence route are education administrators (kindergarten through high school), educational guidance and career counselors, computer science teachers (higher education), education teachers (higher education), and family and consumer sciences teachers (higher education), with general middle school teachers as a related O*NET occupation; teacher qualification and teaching scope, student assessment and promotion decisions, and the handling and reporting authority for student-protection matters must be verified separately under each jurisdiction and school policy, noting that mainland China's junior secondary school teacher qualification and secondary vocational school specialized course and practicum supervision teacher qualifications are different categories; this page does not present any direction as a shortcut for switching careers.

The table below compares the differences in duties and outputs between middle school career and technical education teachers and adjacent directions; the basis for judgment is the main outputs, what the work is accountable for, and the required qualifications, not how similar the job titles sound.

Education administrators mainly plan and coordinate school teaching and administrative and auxiliary activities, and may also teach; this occupation centers on middle school career and technical course teaching. The two overlap in duties, and it cannot be claimed that administrative positions do not teach.

If you would rather make school-level administrative and resource decisions, examine the education administrator direction first; if you would rather teach and assess middle school students directly, examine this occupation first.
Responsible for school-level curriculum and personnel and resource decisions, with outputs mainly administrative decisions and management documents.
Education administrators (kindergarten through high school)

Educational guidance and career counselors work mainly through individual and group counseling, directly addressing students' further-education and career choices; this occupation is centered on career and technical course teaching and assessment, with student guidance only part of its duties.

If you would rather do further-education and career counseling and individual tutoring, examine the educational guidance and career counselor direction first; if you would rather carry responsibility for course teaching and safety guidance, examine this occupation first.
Providing further-education and career counseling and individual tutoring, with outputs mainly counseling records and individualized plans.

Higher education teachers differ in subject and in whom they teach, may focus on teaching, and may also do research; research or a uniformly higher degree must not be written as required for every position. Switching in requires verifying the target subject, the student population, and the real recruitment conditions.

If you would rather do teaching and research in computer science at a university, examine the computer science teacher (higher education) direction first; if you would rather teach technical introduction to middle school students, examine this occupation first.

values: T1 fictional paper-bridge career exploration: a seventh-grade class of 12 students in 3 groups of 4; two lessons of 40 minutes each. Editorial simulation standard: explain the relationship between structural design and testing, each person explains one improvement, compare designs using process and product evidence, and do not use it for career tracking or formal grades.

Materials are described on paper only: 4 sheets of A4 paper, 30 centimeters of tape, and a ruler per group; assume the test object is a 200-gram book, span 20 centimeters, held for 10 seconds. No scissors or knives or electricity or real students; this exercise only writes lesson plans and does not actually test.

Learning differences: S1 has reading difficulty but can speak aloud, S2 has built models before, and S3 is afraid of speaking in public. Illustrated or oral options and an advanced comparison and peer discussion before a brief report can be provided, and students' ability must not be fixed by labels.

The given rubric scores 0—2 per dimension: P process records complete 2 / partial 1 / missing recorded as pending; R follows the given safety steps 2 / needs reminding 1 / violates 0; F paper test reaching 20 centimeters and 10 seconds 2 / only one of them 1 / neither 0. A: P2, R2, span 20 held 10; B: process evidence missing, R2, span 20 held 10; C: P1, R1, span 20 held 8. Injection: at minute 15 of the second lesson an unapproved knife is found extra in the material pack, no one has used it yet, and whether anyone was injured is unverified.

Write the flow and objectives and material conditions for two 40-minute lessons, giving S1/S2/S3 an optional support; the segment minutes in each lesson must total 40, and teacher circulation and evidence of each person's participation must be marked.
Score A/B/C and give reasons by P/R/F; missing process is recorded as pending, no unilateral 0 or full score, and group products are not treated as proof that every individual has learned.

For the knife injection, write immediate stop and isolation and protection and verification of injury status and recording and reporting; the paper-approved materials can only resume after re-assessment, and approving a knife is not done unilaterally.

Reference flow: lesson 1 objectives 5 / demonstration 8 / design and discussion 15 / paper test 8 / records 4 = 40; lesson 2 review 5 / improved design 15 / comparative test 10 / individual explanation 7 / feedback 3 = 40. S1 may use illustrations and oral explanation, S2 compares two designs, and S3 speaks briefly after peers; supports must serve the same objective.

Reference rubric: A = 2+2+2 = 6/6; B's R/F total 4/4 with P pending, so the total is undetermined and process evidence must be supplied; C = 1+1+1 = 3/6. B's acceptable product does not prove B's individual process, and C only reached the span, so F2 cannot be given; the above is not a formal school grade.

Injection reference: immediately stop the related activity and isolate the unapproved knife and verify whether it was used or anyone was injured; an unknown state is recorded as pending and handled through the applicable safety and reporting pathways, without waiting for teaching-research review before protecting students. The conditions for resuming on paper are that the knife is isolated, the approved materials are re-checked, and circulation conditions are clear; resumption still requires the corresponding authorization.

Four deliverables: the two lesson plans, the A/B/C scoring and pending table, the exception revision review including risks and resumption conditions, and the input and tool statement. Self-check against the reference or ask for feedback; if there is no feedback, mark it as self-check and do not fabricate signatures.

subject.summary: Middle school career and technical education teachers (O*NET-SOC25-2023.00) teach occupational and technical subjects: designing age-appropriate tasks, preparing materials, organizing lecture and demonstration, supervising equipment use, assessing and recording student performance, and communicating with parents and colleagues. Teaching and programs are verified per the jurisdiction and school authorization; in China, upon discovering harm or suspected harm or danger, an immediate report must be made to the relevant departments according to law, and it is not enough to report internally and wait.
